patches.text:
% BEGIN readability-patch ov02
The product form comes first, then the four numbered bounds in order.
Conditioning on $H=f$ leaves the two sources running on independent coins, so
their output-leakage pairs factorise; summing out the outputs and dividing by
$\Prob{\vz=\zeta\mid f}$ gives the product $\Pi_{f,\zeta}$. Item~1 is the maximum
of a product measure. Item~2 is proved by exhibiting a predictor that reads all
of $H$, computes $\pi^{i}_{H,z_i}$ and outputs a maximiser, whose success
probability is $\Exp[m_i]$ and which unpredictability bounds by $\delta$.
Item~3 combines Item~2 with $m_2\le1$. Item~4 observes that $m_1m_2>\theta$
forces $m_i>\sqrt\theta$ for one of the two indices, then applies Markov's
inequality to that factor.
% END readability-patch ov02

patches.text:
% BEGIN readability-patch ov04
The four labelled steps of the body are a concentration argument followed by a
union bound, and then two calculations that convert the resulting bound into the
form used later. Step one shows that the event fixing the revealed set and its
values is measurable with respect to $f|_{S_0}$, so conditioning on it leaves the
unrevealed coordinates uniform and freezes $\theta_{\zeta,f}$ and
$p_{\theta_{\zeta,f}}$. Step two applies Hoeffding's inequality to the
independent mean-zero variables $\theta(f(u))-p_\theta$ on $R\setminus S_0$.
Step three multiplies that failure probability by the number of tuples,
$|\mathcal Z|\binom{N}{k_1}\binom{N}{k_2}$, so that the exponential factors
cancel against the definition of $t$, and sums over the $N^{2}$ pairs. Step four
bounds $t$ by $\sqrt{L(m_1+m_2)+2C_0m_1m_2}$ using $1/k_i\le2m_i$, and takes
expectations by concavity of the square root together with the second and third
items of the posterior product structure.
% END readability-patch ov04

patches.text:
% BEGIN readability-patch ov05
The three requirements of a revealing rule are checked in turn. The next
position inspected is a function of $\zeta$ and the values already seen, because
the loop and the representatives $v_j$ are fixed in advance and within run $j$
the next position depends on $(v_j,\zeta)$ and the previous answers. The budget
is $\min(qM',N^{2})$ because each of the $M'$ runs issues at most $q$ positions
and only $N^{2}$ cells exist. For the test, an arbitrary $v$ with $j=h(v)$ makes
$D^{f}(v,\zeta)$ issue exactly the positions of run $j$, all of them recorded,
so the run reconstructs from $(v,\zeta,\mathcal S,f|_{\mathcal S})$ and the whole
function $\theta_{\zeta,f}$ is determined by $(\zeta,\mathcal S,f|_{\mathcal S})$.
% END readability-patch ov05
